title: Snuff at a wake
html_source:
According to the website irishidentity.com, this idiom has an intriguing origin: at a wake,

It was […] customary for a bowl of snuff to be placed on the chest of the dead person. This had a dual function in the snuff being a desirable commodity, brought the mourners close to the coffin to say a prayer for the deceased [sic]. Should the person in the coffin not be dead, the bowl on his or her chest would be seen to rise and fall, though no record exists of anyone being rescued by snuff. So many came forward that the bowl had to be replenished regularly, giving rise to the saying “disappeared like snuff at a wake”.
